## Introduction

This is a basic example of an **R Markdown** document. You can easily format text with *italics*, **bold**, or insert [links](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com). 

Here is a quick bulleted list of features:
* Easy formatting
* Embedded code
* Automatic report generation

## Data Analysis

Below, we embed an R code chunk. It calculates a summary of the built-in `cars` dataset and prints the results directly into our final report.
```{r spec-seed-chunk}
flip <- function(n){
    return(sample(c("H", "T"), n, replace = TRUE))
}

set.seed(4623119)
flip(10)

```

```{r beacr-flip-chunk}
devtools::load_all()
seed = beacr::get_seed()
set.seed(seed)
flip(10)

```

```{r osfr-chunk}
anes_project <- osfr::osf_retrieve_node("https://osf.io/jgyxm")
anes_project_ = osfr::osf_download(osfr::osf_ls_files(anes_project)[4, ], conflict="skip")

csv_path = anes_project_[["local_path"]]

df = read.csv(csv_path)

summary(df)
```

## Data Visualization

We can also include plots. The chunk options `echo=FALSE` tells R Markdown to hide the code itself and only display the resulting graph.

```{r plot-chunk, echo=FALSE}
plot(cars, main = "Speed vs. Stopping Distance")
```
